operation_details.item: The user always chooses only free public data sources for market research and avoids paid databases.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good morning! How’s the budget planning going today?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well. I’m refining the market-sizing section for next quarter’s plan and comparing a few industry trends.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Are you using one of the subscription research platforms, or pulling the data together yourself?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m pulling it together myself. I stick to free public sources for market research rather than using paid databases.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That can work well if you triangulate the numbers. Which sources have been most useful?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Government statistics, company filings, investor presentations, and industry associations. I usually build a range instead of pretending the estimate is perfectly precise.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds practical. Are you planning to include multiple growth scenarios in the budget?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes—base, upside, and a faster-expansion case. I’d rather show the decision-makers the options than bury the upside under overly conservative assumptions.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For market research subscriptions, I always choose only free public data sources and avoid paid databases even when accuracy and timeliness matter.
